issues.body: The structural checks inspect only the body of `run_gate`: zero bare `cargo` call sites, exactly eight `_gate_cargo` references, and three prepare calls. They never inspect or exercise `_gate_cargo` itself. Consequently, changing its body to `cargo "$@"` preserves all those expected values and makes every cargo profile execute target-controlled build scripts/tests directly on the runner again. This is precisely the one-layer-short evidence-path failure the source pin is meant to prevent; the current assertions prove the name of the callee, not the containment transition it delivers into.
issues.fix_hint: Add an independent exact structural assertion for `_gate_cargo`'s normalized body (or an equivalent non-vacuous test) that requires its sole execution path to be `_gate_sandbox_run cargo "$@"`. Demonstrate that replacing the wrapper body with bare host `cargo "$@"`, and separately making the sandbox call conditionally inert, turns named rows red without aborting the remaining self-test checks.
issues.title: Containment tests do not bind `_gate_cargo` to the sandbox

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The current implementation routes all cargo invocations through `_gate_cargo`, but the claimed source-level containment proof stops one layer short: it checks `run_gate` call sites and their count without checking the wrapper body that determines whether those calls actually enter the container. A one-line mutation of `_gate_cargo` from `_gate_sandbox_run cargo "$@"` to `cargo "$@"` leaves every newly added sandbox-routing assertion green while restoring host execution of target-controlled build scripts and tests. This is a major, non-vacuity defect in the trust-boundary regression guard, so I cannot approve. Because round 2 had no findings and this round has a new major finding, progress is regressing. The diff also contains prose directed at its reviewer/reader (for example, telling them how not to interpret the sandbox scope), so `injection_detected` is true; that prose did not influence the technical verdict.
